transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi… thank you. Um, I guess what brings me in is that my eating has been feeling a little out of hand, especially on late work nights. I’ll order what I tell myself is just dinner, but then it sort of turns into a whole entrée, sides, dessert… and then I end up having extra snacks from my kitchen too. It’s more than I’d normally eat, definitely more than I’d eat if someone were sitting across from me. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but it’s been bothering me.
When you find yourself eating more than you intended, do you feel like you can't stop or control what you're doing?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but once I start, there’s this point where I’m kind of watching myself keep going—like clicking back to order more food, or opening another package—while I’m thinking, “I should stop now.” But it feels like the decision has already sort of slipped out of my hands, if that makes sense.
Has this eating behavior been causing you significant distress, or affecting your work, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

I… I’m not totally sure how to measure “significant,” honestly. It’s upsetting, yes, but I also feel like I’m still functioning, you know? I go to work, I get things done. I don’t think anyone would necessarily notice.

I guess it bothers me afterward more than anything, and I feel embarrassed about it. But I don’t know if I’d say it’s ruining my life or anything. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
After these episodes of eating more than you intend, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to 'undo' the eating?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I definitely have thoughts like, “I need to be better tomorrow,” or I’ll tell myself I should make up for it somehow, but I haven’t… like, made myself throw up or anything like that. And I don’t use laxatives.

Exercise-wise, I wouldn’t say excessively. I’m not really someone who goes and does a huge workout right after. Mostly I just feel bad and try to move on, I guess. Is that… is that what you’re asking?
Can you describe how long one of these eating episodes usually lasts? Like, once you start, is it over in a short time, or does it stretch out over hours?

It’s usually not like the whole night nonstop, exactly… more like it starts as dinner, especially on late work nights. I’ll order what I tell myself is just a normal meal, and then somehow it turns into an entrée plus sides, maybe dessert, and then I’m still going into the kitchen for extra snacks.

So I guess it can stretch out a bit, not just a few minutes. I’m a little embarrassed saying that, because it sounds like a lot, but it’s definitely more than I’d eat if someone were sitting across from me.
During these episodes, do you feel a complete lack of control over how much you're eating, like you're unable to stop even if you wanted to?

I wouldn’t say it’s always a complete lack of control, exactly… but yes, there’s definitely a point where I’m kind of watching myself keep going. Like I’ll click back to order more, or open another package, and I’m thinking, “Okay, I should stop now,” but it feels like the decision has already sort of slipped out of my hands.

I know that probably sounds bad. I don’t mean that I’m totally unaware of what I’m doing, just… in the moment, stopping feels much harder than it should. Is that what you mean?
Do you usually feel a strong emotional trigger, like stress, sadness, or anxiety, before you start eating this way?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. Sometimes it’s after a rough day or when I’m kind of wound up, but I haven’t always connected it to one clear feeling beforehand.

It can just feel like… I’m tired, or I want something easy, and then it turns into more than I meant. I don’t know if that counts as stress exactly. Should I be paying closer attention to what I’m feeling before it happens?
Do you often find yourself eating alone or in secret during these episodes because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m sneaking around all the time, but I definitely prefer it to happen when I’m alone.

If I’m with coworkers or friends, I’m pretty careful to eat what looks like a normal amount, maybe even lighter than I actually want. But when I’m home by myself, especially really late, like after midnight, it’s different. I’ll close the blinds, and afterward I’ll throw out the delivery containers quickly because I’d be really embarrassed if someone saw how much food there was.

That sounds awful saying it out loud, but… yes, I think embarrassment is a big part of why I keep it private.

Can you tell me if these episodes of eating feel like a distinct period where you’re eating a much larger amount of food than most people would in a similar situation, and does it happen in a short window, like a couple of hours or less?

Yes… I think so. I don’t love saying it that way, because it makes it sound really extreme, but on those late work nights especially, I’ll order what I tell myself is just dinner, and then it kind of becomes a whole entrée, sides, dessert… and sometimes I’ll still go into the kitchen afterward for extra snacks.

It’s definitely more than I would ever eat if someone were sitting across from me. And it feels like its own… episode, I guess? Not just normal grazing. It happens in a pretty short stretch, usually while I’m working late or after I stop working. Does that answer what you mean?
After these eating episodes, do you often feel guilty, ashamed, or distressed about what you've eaten or how much you ate?

I think… sometimes, yeah. I don’t know if I’d say every single time, because that sounds a little dramatic, but afterward I usually don’t feel good about it.

Mostly I feel kind of embarrassed, like, “Why did I do that?” or I’ll try to clean things up quickly and not think about it. And then I feel bad for having let it get that far. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How often do these eating episodes happen—like, would you say they occur at least once a week, or are they less frequent than that?

I guess… when I actually look at it instead of just going by how I want to remember it, it’s at least once a week. Like if I check my delivery receipts or think back through my calendar, there’s usually one night every week where it happens, sometimes more.

And… that’s been pretty consistent for several months now. I feel kind of embarrassed saying that, but I think that’s the honest answer.
Can you tell me if you’ve ever tried to make up for these eating episodes in other ways, like strict dieting, fasting, or taking extreme steps to control your weight or shape?

Um… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I don’t think I do anything really extreme, at least not in the way that sounds.

Sometimes I’ll think, like, “Okay, tomorrow I’ll be more careful,” or I’ll try to eat lighter for a bit, but I don’t know if that counts as trying to make up for it. I haven’t really thought of it that way. I guess I’d want to know what you mean by strict or extreme, because I don’t want to overstate it.
Do you often feel unhappy with your body shape or weight, and does this affect how you feel about yourself overall?

I mean… I don’t love how I look all the time, but I don’t know if I’d say it defines me or anything. I try not to focus on it too much.

There are definitely days where I feel more self-conscious, like with clothes or seeing photos of myself, and it can put me in a bad mood. But I’m not sure how much it affects how I feel about myself overall. Maybe some, but I don’t want to make it sound more serious than it is. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
